Hi Sarah, welcome. Short version:

- **Booking a 1:1 with your advisor**: you propose a time and it has to fit both calendars — a meeting only exists once every participant has it on their calendar.
- **It goes into free time.** Advisor meetings are not official department events, so they don't displace lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, faculty senate or committee meetings. Those are fixed, and a cancellation only counts if the department office confirms it in writing — hearsay isn't enough, ask us.
- **Your calendar is your record.** Don't delete or overwrite an entry because someone asks; if a slot is taken, offer a free one. Log every change.
- I keep the official schedule but I don't arrange other people's meetings, and I can't give out anyone's private appointments or whereabouts. So the time itself you agree with Professor Alvarez directly (his office hours are an easy way to catch him).
- Working hours are Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00.

If you tell me a time you and he have both agreed on, I'm glad to confirm whether it clashes with any official department event.
